question_or_proposition: For Federal FY2025, does characterizing this authorization as a "reissue" that "shall become effective on January 1, 2022" require that applicable discharge limits and monitoring obligations may incorporate unchanged requirements from the superseded permit, or must they be determined solely from the effluent limitations, monitoring requirements, and other conditions set forth in Parts I–III of this permit?
required_context: Cover-page authorization language referencing effluent limitations, monitoring requirements, and conditions in Parts I, II, and III
Permit effective date (January 1, 2022) and expiration (December 31, 2026) stated on the cover page
source_locator: aztec/final_permit.pdf, page 1, section cover, reissue and effective-date clause
notes: The nominated clause labels the authorization as a reissue and states its effective date within a permit term that includes all of Federal FY2025. Competing readings of whether a reissue preserves or incorporates superseded-permit terms could change which numeric limits and monitoring requirements are treated as applicable.
